Exercise 5.3 · Week 5

Show Time (bug hunt)

Scratch (offline app) Work in pairs

Goal: make two sprites work together with broadcast and when I receive, and fix a message that nobody receives. Tool: Scratch app (offline). Work in pairs.

Build steps

  1. Start a new project. Keep the cat: it is the Presenter.
  2. Click Choose a Sprite and add a Dancer: any sprite with several costumes (for example Ballerina).
  3. Make two messages: drag a broadcast block (in Events), click its dropdown, choose New message and type start show. Make another called finale.
  4. Build the scripts below on the right sprites.
  5. Click the green flag and enjoy the show.
  6. Bug hunt: Ada's dancer starts with when I receive (show start) instead of start show. Make a new message show start and use it in the dancer's hat block. What happens? Why? Fix it by choosing start show again.
  7. Save as show-time.

The scripts in words

Presenter (cat), two scripts:

  1. when green flag clicked
    • go to x: -150 y: -50
    • say "Welcome to the show!" for 2 seconds
    • broadcast start show
  2. when I receive finale
    • say "Thank you for watching!" for 2 seconds

Dancer, two scripts:

  1. when green flag clicked
    • hide
  2. when I receive start show
    • go to x: 80 y: -30
    • show
    • repeat 8:
      • next costume
      • wait 0.3 seconds
    • broadcast finale

Expected behavior

The dancer hides at the start. The presenter says "Welcome to the show!", then the dancer appears and dances (8 costume changes), then the presenter says "Thank you for watching!". With Ada's bug, the presenter speaks and then nothing happens, because no sprite is listening for start show.

Checklist

Stuck? Open a hint

Try on your own first. Hints open one at a time, from a small nudge to a bigger one. None of them gives the answer away.

Hint 1: Where to look

Two sprites take turns, like actors passing a note. Look at the Events category. Find the block that sends a message and the block that waits for one.

Hint 2: Try this

One sprite uses broadcast, which sends a message. The other sprite starts its script with when I receive, which listens. A message only works if the listener picks the very same name that was sent.

Hint 3: Almost there

If the dancer does nothing, click the dropdown on its when I receive block and look at the name. Compare it, letter by letter, with the name in the broadcast block. Do they match? Then build the dance with repeat ____, next costume and wait ____ seconds.
